feed.title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Partner: AI Risks Leaving the Next Generation of Bankers Unable to Think for Themselves
feed.summary: A Goldman Sachs partner, Chris Churchman, has warned that the widespread adoption of AI on Wall Street could diminish the reasoning skills of future bankers, comparing it to how GPS eroded navigation abilities. While AI offers immediate productivity benefits for the firm, there's a concern that it might hinder the development of junior bankers' judgment, as much of banking knowledge is gained through hands-on experience. Despite acknowledging this talent risk, Goldman Sachs has not yet outlined a clear strategy to mitigate these long-term consequences amidst competitive pressure from other financial institutions also deploying AI tools.

feed.title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Partner: AI Risks Leaving the Next Generation of Bankers Unable to Think for Themselves
feed.summary: A Goldman Sachs partner, Chris Churchman, has warned that the widespread use of AI in banking risks eroding the reasoning skills of future bankers, potentially leading to "cognitive atrophy." While AI offers immediate productivity benefits and is being integrated into platforms like Marquee, Churchman emphasizes the long-term structural risk of junior bankers not developing critical judgment if AI handles routine tasks. The firm acknowledges this talent risk but has not yet identified a clear mitigation strategy, raising concerns about its ability to maintain talent development amidst competitive pressure.

feed.title: California Democrats panic as PG&E cuts $2 billion in planned spending over wildfire liability fight
feed.summary: PG&E announced it would cut $2 billion in planned 2027 investments, citing the financial burden of California's wildfire-liability rules. The move comes after lawmakers failed to agree on a liability overhaul that would have shifted wildfire costs, leaving utilities, insurers, and lawmakers in a standoff.
